briefings.headline: The Sensex jumped 773 points to 81,879, its highest close since February, and the Nifty topped 25,250 as PSU banks and carmakers led and foreign money kept flowing in; Blackstone agreed to invest ₹5,000 crore in IIFL Finance, and the rupee firmed to 93.70.

The Sensex rose 107 points to 81,107 and the Nifty held above 25,000 in a choppy session as state-run banks jumped and IT shares slipped; Citi raised its Nifty target to 28,000, HSBC upgraded India, and the rupee edged up to 93.93 as oil eased.

The Sensex jumped 1,718 points to 81,028 for a seventh straight gain and the Nifty reclaimed 25,000 as banks led and foreign money poured in, even as US and Asian markets crashed on AI fears; M&M's profit rose 25%, and the rupee gained 52 paise to 93.89.

The Sensex jumped 2,009 points to 79,310 for a sixth straight gain after oil crashed nearly 9% on hopes the US may seek an end to the Iran war; auto and finance shares led, Titan's profit rose 54%, and the rupee held at 94.46.

The Sensex rose 383 points to 77,301 for a fifth straight gain as smaller companies and media shares led after Democrats won the US Congress; BEL jumped 4.71%, IT shares fell, and the rupee gained 17 paise to 94.58.

The Sensex rose 1,225 points to 76,917 for a fourth straight gain, led by FMCG shares as Marico jumped 10%; SBI fell despite a 14% profit rise, broker shares rallied on tax hopes, and the rupee gained 13 paise to 94.71.

The Sensex jumped 1,233 points to 75,692 as Reliance soared 11.6% after record profits and oil fell about 4% on Iran-Qatar peace talks; SEBI reportedly asked for a tax cut for foreign investors, and the rupee slipped 10 paise to 94.86.

The Sensex rose 308 points to 74,459 as IT and pharma shares and strong results from Trent and IndiGo offset falls in smaller shares; the rupee jumped 33 paise to 94.93 while oil rose on fears of new US strikes on Iran.

The Sensex jumped 905 points to 74,151 after the US Fed held rates, oil slipped to about $114 and hopes of a capital gains tax cut lifted banks, realty and FMCG shares; the rupee edged up 3 paise to 95.25.

The Sensex fell 353 points as Infosys, Reliance and oil companies slid with Brent near $115, but Jio Platforms closed about 27% above its IPO price on its first day and L&T jumped after a 33% profit rise; the rupee fell to 95.28.

The Sensex ended flat, down just 8 points, as bank and IT shares slipped while smallcaps jumped about 2.7% on expiry day; Tata Consumer rose after a 16% profit rise, and Jio Platforms lists on Wednesday.

The Sensex rose 483 points to end a four-day losing streak as metal and pharma shares led a broad recovery, but the rupee fell 29 paise past 95 per dollar; Jio IPO allotment was due today ahead of Wednesday's listing.

The Sensex slipped 126 points for a fourth day of losses, but smaller shares fell about 2% to 3% as oil climbed above $114; the Jio IPO drew heavy bids on its last day and Infosys cut its growth forecast.

The Sensex fell 460 points for a third day of losses as oil rose above $110 after a drone attack near a Saudi oilfield and Asian markets slid; the Jio IPO's retail portion was fully booked and the rupee fell 44 paise.

The Sensex slipped 143 points as oil rose above $110 and smaller company shares slumped, while IT shares jumped; the Jio Platforms IPO was fully subscribed within about 100 minutes and the rupee rose to a six-week high.

The Sensex fell 876 points as private bank shares slid after HDFC Bank and Axis Bank results showed thinner lending margins; big investors bid for the Jio Platforms IPO ahead of Wednesday's opening, and the rupee ended a six-day winning run.

The Sensex rose 414 points for a second day of gains as IT shares jumped almost 4% after strong results from Tech Mahindra, which also announced bonus shares; the rupee rose for a sixth day and SEBI finalised new closing-price rules.

The Sensex jumped 1,534 points as IT, bank and Reliance shares rallied on cheaper oil and Jio's IPO plans, even as most smaller shares fell and Asian markets plunged on AI worries; the rupee rose for a fifth day.
Wholesale inflation jumped to 11.39% in September and the Sensex slipped 252 points as pharma shares fell and investors waited for US inflation data; the rupee rose for a fourth day.
The Sensex jumped 1,109 points as the Finance Minister said she was open to views on taxes on share-market profits and IT shares surged after HCLTech's results; the rupee rose for a third day.

Retail inflation jumped to 5.54% in September and government bond yields hit a three-year high; the Sensex fell 548 points even as the rupee had its best day in over six months after RBI curbs on speculation.

The RBI raised its main interest rate for the first time since 2023, to 5.50%, and said cuts are off the table for now; the Sensex fell 429 points as loan-linked shares slipped and the rupee neared its record low.

Indian shares rose for a second day as oil slipped below $100 and strong early figures from Trent and Kotak Mahindra Bank lifted the mood; the Sensex gained 685 points a day before the RBI's rate decision.
Indian shares broke a four-day losing run after weak US jobs data cut the odds of a US rate hike and oil eased; the Sensex rose 473 points as the RBI began its three-day rate meeting.
Indian shares fell for a fourth day as auto stocks slumped on disappointing September sales, foreign investors kept selling and the rupee slid to a two-month low of 96.31 per dollar.
Indian shares fell for a third day after an early rally faded, as hospital stocks slumped on Supreme Court remarks about medicine prices and oil rose again; the rupee gained 13 paise.
Indian shares slipped for a second day as oil stayed near $107 and US bond yields hit a 19-year high, with IT and consumer goods companies leading the fall.
Indian shares fell about 1.5% to near six-month lows after the US rejected Iran's offer to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, sending oil back above $107 and the rupee past 96 per dollar.
Indian shares bounced back a little on bargain hunting and slightly cheaper oil, but the Nifty still ended its seventh losing week in a row.
Indian shares fell sharply as US borrowing costs hit a 19-year high, oil stayed above $100 and a new insurance proposal hit financial stocks.
